topic: Pure Fourier Series: The DNA of Waves

sections.title: Introduction: The Secret Recipe of Sounds
lecture_lines: Any complex periodic signal contains hidden pure waves.
Melody-Bot uses tuning forks to recreate a messy buzz.
Combining pure notes yields the original complex sound.
animations: Complex buzzing wave (jagged #FF5555 line) appears and oscillates.
Character 'Melody-Bot' appears holding three white (#FFFFFF) tuning forks.
Three pure sine waves (#55FF55) merge to recreate the buzzing sound.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Pure Wave
lecture_lines: Sine waves are defined by height, speed, and phase.
Rotation on a circle generates these fundamental oscillations.
Pure waves of different frequencies never interfere with identity.
animations: Circle with rotating red dot (#FF0000) traces a sine wave.
Labels for Amplitude (height) and Frequency (rotation speed) appear in #FFFFFF.
Two waves (#FFFF00 and #00FFFF) show different frequencies sin(x), sin(2x).

sections.title: The Big Idea: Superposition
lecture_lines: Superposition allows us to stack separate pure waves.
Watch how three distinct frequencies align vertically.
We add their heights together at every single point.
The sum forms a new, more complex wave shape.
More frequencies make the approximation even more accurate.
animations: Three separate sine waves (#FF00FF, #00FF00, #0000FF) display vertically.
Vertical height lines appear at a specific point on all waves.
The three waves collapse toward a single horizontal baseline.
Heights of waves are summed at every point along the x-axis.
Resultant wave (#FFFFFF) takes a rough, bumpy square shape.

sections.title: The Mathematical Blueprint
lecture_lines: The Fourier formula provides a mathematical recipe for waves.
The constant term represents the wave's average height.
Coefficients a-n and b-n act like volume sliders.
They determine the strength of each cosine and sine.
This blueprint reconstructs any periodic function precisely.
animations: The Fourier Series formula appears in white (#FFFFFF) text.
The DC offset term 'a\u2080/2' highlights in Gold (#FFD700).
Term 'a\u2099' and 'b\u2099' transform into interactive green (#00FF00) sliders.
One slider moves up, increasing the magnitude of sin(3x) component.
Total sum wave adjusts its shape according to the slider movement.

sections.title: Case Study: Building a Square Wave
lecture_lines: Let's build a square wave using only odd harmonics.
We start with a single fundamental sine wave.
Adding the third harmonic begins sharpening the corners.
Successive harmonics flatten the peaks and steepen the edges.
Summing to infinity creates a perfect robotic square.
animations: A single white (#FFFFFF) sine wave, sin(x), oscillates.
The 3rd harmonic, sin(3x)/3, is added to the first wave.
The 5th and 7th harmonics are added, sharpening the wave's corners.
Corners of the wave highlight in orange (#FF4500) to show overshoot.
Sequence continues to 20 terms, forming a sharp square wave.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Impact
lecture_lines: Fourier analysis decomposes signals into their constituent DNA.
Prisms of math reveal the hidden frequencies inside data.
This compression enables modern music and digital imaging.
animations: Complex wave enters a gray (#AAAAAA) triangular prism.
Sequence of pure sine waves exits the prism at different angles.
Icons for MP3 and JPEG appear next to the sine waves.
